# Categorization rules: priority ordering (v2)

Thread: marc://$categorization-rules-priority-ordering-0d4f9b13

Closed: `2026-06-03T12:00:00.000Z`

---

## Scope

When two rules in the rules engine match the same transaction, the result must not depend on the order of the lines in the rule file. This thread adds an explicit priority to each rule of the engine, so that the category of a transaction is decided by the rule definitions and not by where a line happens to sit in the file. It builds on the regex matching of version one, which remains unchanged.

## Ordering

Each rule receives a numeric priority. The engine sorts the rules by priority and then by rule identifier, and the first matching rule wins. Rules without a priority receive the default value defined in the rule schema. The position of a line in the file plays no role in the result, which makes the behavior the same whether the file is edited by hand or generated by a tool.

## Decisions

Priority belongs to the rule itself, not to its place in the file. Equal priorities are broken by the identifier, so the order stays stable across reloads and across machines. This keeps the outcome predictable when a user reorders the lines of the file or adds a new rule at the top of it.

## Outcome

A reload test shuffles the rule file and checks that every sample transaction still receives the category it received before the shuffle. The thread closed after that test passed and the rule schema documentation was updated to describe the default priority.
